title: Adaptive Schema Anchors: SDK Streaming + Tool Call Playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose
---
Working PRD sketch describing a pragmatic approach for reliably emitting partial structured outputs during streaming responses while supporting tool-calls and preserving ergonomics for client SDKs. This doc experiments with the concept of 'schema anchors' — lightweight markers baked into streaming frames that give clients a stable, evolvable contract for incremental parsing and graceful fallback.

Problem statement
---
- Customers building real-time apps need structured pieces of output (entities, action objects, tool call intents) as earliest-possible events.
- Current partial JSON / incremental strategies are brittle: small model phrasing changes, tokenization cutoff, or network truncation can produce invalid fragments.
- SDKs try to parse partial text streams but end up with complex client-side heuristics and edge-case bugs (double-processing, tool-dupe, partial-commit races).
- We need a minimal, low-latency protocol that: preserves streaming speed, reduces client parsing complexity, and admits server-side validation and safe rollback semantics.

Goals
---
1) Provide a streaming frame format that makes it straightforward for SDKs to surface partial structured outputs (anchors) with sanity checks.
2) Support tool calls emitted mid-stream with atomicity guarantees (at-most-once invocation or clear retry semantics).
3) Make the protocol backward-friendly and tolerant to model variants and partial frame loss.
4) Keep SDK ergonomics simple: small surface changes for existing clients, well-documented failure modes, and clear migrations.

Non-goals
---
- This PRD does not propose changing billing semantics or major server-side batching heuristics.
- Not trying to standardize a full JSON-LD schema for all customers. We propose lightweight anchors plus optional customer-provided schema templates.

User scenarios
---
- Live coding assistant that displays function call suggestions as the model composes; the client should be able to render a callable button as soon as the model signals an action anchor.
- Customer support tool that needs early entity extraction to pre-fill forms while the rest of the message is still being generated.
- Mobile composition UI that must not block on full generation to offer progressive autocomplete.

Design: concept overview
---
- Schema anchor: a small, unambiguous frame inserted into the token stream announcing a structured fragment. Anchors are syntactic delimiters plus a compact checksum/shape hint (not the full payload).
- Anchor types: ACTION, ENTITY_PART, CHECKPOINT, TOOL_CALL_INTENT. Each anchor type has a minimal header: anchor-id, type, seq (monotonic per-response), checksum-hint, optional schema-id (customer-supplied or platform template).
- Anchor payload: immediately following the header the model may stream the payload bytes. Payload may be partial; the anchor header signals how to reconcile partials (append mode, replace mode, confirm-only).
- Fallback path: when an anchor payload fails checksum or is truncated, SDKs fall back to "tentative" UI states and request either a completion frame or server-side repair API.

Streaming handshake (SDK <-> Hosted API)
---
- Client can opt-in using request param: streaming_schema=true and optionally supply schema templates (schema_id list).
- Server returns initial handshake frame: session_token, server_supported_anchor_types, max_anchor_size. This is first frame in stream.
- Anchor frame format (text-transport): ANCHOR|<anchor-id>|<type>|<seq>|<schema-id>|<checksum-hint>
  - Example: ANCHOR|a83f|ACTION|12|fn-spec-v1|c4d1
- Immediately after header, server may stream payload lines until an ANCHOR-END marker or until sequence advances.
- Clients acknowledge receipt of completed anchors via lightweight ACK frames over the same connection if they want reliable at-most-once semantics for tool invocations. ACK is optional for faster paths.

Tool-call semantics
---
- Tool call should be explicit: an ACTION anchor with schema-id referencing platform function specification (input/output shapes).
- At-most-once: to avoid duplicate invocation on retries, tool invocation happens only after the client or server has observed an ACTION anchor checksum match and the server emits a TOOL-COMMIT frame with invocation-id. Alternatively, clients may request server-side pre-commit by sending a client ACK.
- Retry semantics: if the connection drops before TOOL-COMMIT, the client may re-open the session and request server replay from last checkpoint sequence. Server may decline to re-invoke if commit was ambiguous (server indicates ambiguity in replay response).

Structured output reconciliation
---
- Checkpoint anchors: model emits a CHECKPOINT anchor periodically that includes a lightweight snapshot hash of the current reconstructed structured state. Server keeps short-lived checkpoint logs for session replay and repair.
- Partial merges: ENTITY_PART anchors include instructions (append/merge/replace). SDK applies merge heuristics that are deterministic and documented.
- Repair API: POST /repair-session {session, seq} -> attempts server-side re-synthesis of missing/invalid anchor payloads and returns repaired anchor frames. Useful for long-tail cases where client cannot safely display a partial.

SDK ergonomics guidance
---
Primary principles:
- Keep user-facing API surface minimal: 1) stream(handler) 2) onAnchor(type, callback) 3) commitAck(anchor-id) optional 4) repair() helper.
- Default behavior: SDK surfaces anchors as "tentative" objects; apps may opt into auto-commit for ACTION anchors.
- Provide two programming models: optimistic (show early, call tool on accept) and conservative (wait for TOOL-COMMIT).
- Error modes: SDK should emit events: anchorInvalid, anchorRepairRequested, anchorCommitted, anchorAmbiguous. Document recommended UI states for each event.

Server-side implementation notes (ops/infra)
---
- Anchors must be compact and easily tokenizable by decoders; avoid long delimiters that hurt thread scheduling in runtime.
- Keep anchor parsing in the early stage of the serving runtime to enable prefix caching and cheap checksum verification without full decode.
- Checkpoint logs are short-lived (default retention 2 minutes) to support fast replays without persistence costs. Configurable per-tenant for Dedicated/Private.
- Instrument counters: anchors_emitted_total, anchors_repaired_total, tool_commits_total, anchor_checksum_failures.

Telemetry and metrics
---
Success metrics (initial 8 weeks):
- Anchor delivery rate >= 99.2% (anchors emitted that pass checksum on first stream).
- Tool-call commit latency median < 200ms after anchor arrival for optimized flow.
- Repair API usage < 0.5% of sessions for default templates.
- SDK-side anchor parsing errors < 0.2% of anchors.
Operational metrics to track:
- anchors_per_session, avg_anchor_size, anchor_checksum_failures, repair_success_rate, client_ack_rate.

Migration and compatibility
---
- Backwards compatibility: if streaming_schema=false, server behaves current way (no anchors emitted). Clients that don't understand anchors ignore any textual delimiters (we keep anchors printable and bracketed).
- Feature gates: rollout under flag streaming_schema_v1. Default off for GA. Early access via sample customers.

Security and Safety considerations
---
- Anchors should never contain executable code. ACTION anchor payload referencing function names must be validated against tenant allowlist.
- Tool commit flow must verify caller permissions (auth tokens), and server must require explicit signed ACK for high-risk tool calls where at-most-once matters.

Open questions / tradeoffs
---
- Where to put heavy repair logic: best-effort server-side re-synthesis vs. instruct model to re-emit anchor on replay. Cost implication of keeping checkpoints.
- Should we standardize a richer anchor schema (JSON-schema subset) or keep it intentionally small to iterate fast?
- UX patterns for ambiguous commits: immediate disable of call button vs. deferred retry options.

Next steps / short-term roadmap (quarterly):
- Week 0-2: proto SDK + server-side minimal anchor injector + integration test harness (Ravi + Diego).
- Week 3-5: internal dogfood with 2 sandbox customers (Sofia to coordinate).
- Week 6-8: telemetry collection, repair API perf tuning, update docs and SDK samples.
- Week 9: decide GA readiness and billing considerations.

Appendix: example stream trace (toy)
---
[HANDSHAKE] {session: s_21, features: [ANCHORS:ACTION,ENTITY_PART,CHECKPOINT], max_anchor=8KB}
text: "Hi I'm pulling up the..."
ANCHOR|b01|ENTITY_PART|3|ent-v1|9f2a
{ "entity": "Acme Corp", "confidence": 0.87 }
ANCHOR-END|b01
text: "...and I recommend calling"
ANCHOR|b02|ACTION|4|fn-sendSummary-v1|d5c8
{ "function": "sendSummary", "args": {"recipient":"ops@acme.com"} }
ANCHOR-END|b02
TOOL-COMMIT|inv-4493|b02|ok
CHECKPOINT|seq:12|hash:3b9f
text: "done"

Notes to reviewers
---
- This is a rough sketch intended to provoke implementation tradeoffs. Focus review on SDK surface complexity and the repair flow.
- Recommended next meeting: sync with serving runtime (Diego) and SDK owners (Ravi) to validate parsing costs and handshake semantics.
